name: Editorial Desk
icp_fit: World's leading architectural platform (DA 92). Features climate-responsive and vernacular sustainable design case studies.
pitch_angle: Empirical thermal comfort study: Rammed earth vs RCC in Western India summer heat.
pitch_subject: Article idea: Passive cooling & rammed earth lessons from Western India
pitch_body:
Hi ArchDaily Editorial Team,

I follow your sustainability section closely and genuinely love how you highlight climate-responsive architecture from across the globe.

I'm an architect at Anvitam Studio in Western India specializing in bioclimatic and rammed-earth design. We recently completed an empirical study comparing indoor temperatures between stabilized rammed earth and conventional RCC in 42°C summer heat, with comfort metrics achieved without active AC.

We have photography, section drawings, and thermal data ready. I’d love to share an overview if this resonates with your readers:
https://www.anvitam.com/blog

Best,
Archana Gavas
Founder & Principal Architect, Anvitam
https://www.anvitam.com

name: Features Editor
source_name: Centre for Science and Environment (CSE) Submissions
icp_fit: India's premier environmental publication (DA 78). Covers decentralized water systems, ecological architecture, and rural habitats.
pitch_angle: Zero-chemical constructed wetland reed beds for decentralized rural farmstead wastewater.
pitch_subject: Story idea: Zero-chemical reed bed water recycling for rural farmsteads
pitch_body:
Hi Down To Earth Editorial Team,

I've been a reader of CSE's work on groundwater resilience and decentralized ecology for years.

I'm an ecological architect based in Vadodara. Over the past two seasons, our studio has been implementing zero-chemical constructed wetland reed beds for rural retreats and farmsteads—recycling 100% of greywater directly into aquifer recharge using local Phragmites root zones.

We've documented the installation costs and species selection into a visual case study:
https://www.anvitam.com/projects

Would you be open to seeing a short pitch for your upcoming sustainable habitat coverage?

Best,
Archana Gavas
Principal Architect, Anvitam
https://www.anvitam.com
